title: Lumina: Real-Time Neural Rendering by Exploiting Computational Redundancy
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) neural rendering is computationally demanding for mobile SoCs, with high rasterization costs and redundant computation across temporally-coherent frames preventing real-time performance.
motivation: As neural rendering becomes central to AR/VR on mobile devices, the gap between 3DGS compute demands and mobile SoC capabilities must be closed through algorithm-hardware co-design.
method: Lumina renders 3D scenes by blending thousands of Gaussians (fuzzy 3D spheres). Exploiting temporal coherence—the fact that consecutive video frames look almost identical—S2 (Spatial-temporal Skipping) avoids recalculating Gaussian contributions that haven't changed between frames. RC (Radiance Caching) stores intermediate color calculations to skip redundant rasterization work. LuminCore, a purpose-built mobile accelerator, is co-designed to efficiently support these cache lookups and eliminate bottlenecks in standard 3DGS rendering on mobile SoCs.
key_novelty: The core insight is that most computation repeats across consecutive video frames, so Lumina combines S2 (Spatial-temporal Skipping to skip unchanged Gaussians) and RC (Radiance Caching to reuse calculated colors), enabled by a custom mobile accelerator (LuminCore).
contributions: S2 algorithm exploiting temporal coherence to skip redundant Gaussian rendering computations
RC (Radiance Caching) mechanism reducing rasterization frequency by caching color integration results
LuminCore accelerator architecture optimized for cache lookup and efficient 3DGS rasterization on mobile SoCs
4.5x speedup and 5.3x energy reduction vs. mobile Volta GPU with less than 0.2 dB PSNR loss

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 5.3x energy reduction over mobile Volta GPU

limitations: Evaluation is restricted to 3DGS neural rendering; generality to other neural radiance field representations is not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-algorithm co-design for real-time 3DGS neural rendering on mobile SoCs
